text:
alex: heads up — saw 3 GPUs in warm-pool go NotReady after the us-west1 network flap at ~08:12 UTC. pods didn't reschedule, still bound to drained nodes :confused:
mei: ugh. were they actually drained or evicted?
alex: nodes got cordoned by node-drain controller, then the kubelet lost API server during cooldown window. no graceful teardown logs.
ron: that sounds like the cooldown timer running but webhook/cordon succeeded then network interrupted before eviction completed. we might be leaking reserved GPUs.
maria: how many warm-pool instances impacted?
alex: 3 of 12 in gpustack-warmpool-usw. Autoscaler thinks capacity is fine because warmpool counts as available, but scheduler can't place new pods on them.
jamal: can we reproduce locally with simulated API flaps? would be useful to add robustness tests.
mei: yes — I can script a simulated apiserver outage and run the drain + cooldown flow. will try today.
will: quick mitigation — we can reduce warm-pool cooldown to 30s in that pool until we have a fix? downside: more churn.
ron: noted. i'm more worried about the orphaned-device state on nodes. kubelet shows GPUs occupied by stale container processes in `/var/lib/containerd`. scripting a forced cleanup on reconnect might help.
sre-bot: incident created: INC-2026-230 — "warmpool-orphaned-gpus-us-west1". Pager muted for now.
mei: patch idea: when cordon succeeds but kubelet disconnects within cooldown window, mark node as forcibly drained after N retries and enqueue a cleanup job to free device mounts.
maria: we should also update the autoscaler probe logic so it doesn't count cordoned-but-unreachable warm nodes as available. that would avoid hiding capacity shortfalls.
jamal: agree. autoscaler currently queries node conditions via API server; if API flaky it assumes last-known state. we can add a liveness probe TTL override for warmpool nodes.
alex: logging snippet from the node when it happened:
```
Jun 10 08:12:13 kubelet[2345]: Wrote cordon state to API
Jun 10 08:12:14 kubelet[2345]: Starting graceful pod eviction (cooldown 300s)
Jun 10 08:12:17 kubelet[2345]: Error: apiserver unreachable (dial tcp 10.0.0.5:6443: i/o timeout)
Jun 10 08:12:17 kubelet[2345]: Eviction halted, kubelet offline
```
ron: that matches. kubelet can't finish eviction, but cordon prevents scheduler from placing replacements. cluster thinks resources are reserved.
mei: proposal: (1) add a small local watchdog that will forcibly kill containerd GPU processes if kubelet hasn't reconnected after 60s while node is cordoned by our controller; (2) add autoscaler TTL so nodes with last-seen > 45s are treated as unavailable for scheduling.
will: +1 on autoscaler change. but we need to be careful in high-latency regions to not double-scale. maybe make it configurable per-region.
maria: also add metric `warmpool.node_unreachable_seconds` and an alert if > 30s for > 2 nodes in an AZ. ops runbook update please.
jamal: for the runbook: steps to manually reclaim:
```
# on control-plane host
kubectl get nodes -l pool=warm-gpu -o wide
kubectl cordon <node>
# force cleanup on worker
ssh worker && sudo systemctl stop kubelet && sudo pkill -9 containerd && sudo rm -rf /var/lib/containerd/io.containerd.runtime.v2.task/*gpu* && sudo systemctl start containerd && sudo systemctl start kubelet
kubectl uncordon <node>
```
alex: ack — add small note to avoid `pkill` unless on rollback window.
mei: i'll open two PRs: one for autoscaler TTL tweak + per-region flag, one for the local watchdog. will include unit + chaos tests.
ron: please include a simulation in the chaos suite where apiserver delay = 90s and we assert no warmpool leak.
maria: timeline?
mei: autoscaler TTL PR by EOD tomorrow, watchdog WIP by Friday.
jamal: i'll prepare the runbook change and a remediation script in ops repo.
sre-bot: update: INC-2026-230 status changed to "monitoring".
will: thanks team — let's keep an eye on us-west1 metrics for the next 6 hours.
alex: thanks all. :thumbsup:
